-102.36600,31.85110.name: Advanced Fertility Centers, PLLC
-102.36600,31.85110.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Rizwan Malik, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-1.57766,53.73579.name: CREATE Fertility, Leeds
-1.57766,53.73579.state: Capitol Park East, 1 Sterling Way, Topcliffe Lane, Morley, Leeds, West Yorkshire, WF3 1BU
-1.57766,53.73579.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-77.10800,38.99850.name: Recombinant DNA Advisory Committee — archive
-77.10800,38.99850.state: Bethesda — NIH Office of Science Policy, 6705 Rockledge Dr
-77.10800,38.99850.desc: The archive of the committee that oversaw early US genetic engineering, created after scientists themselves called for a moratorium at Asilomar in 1975. It is the record of a field agreeing to pause and then designing its own oversight, and of what happened to that oversight afterwards.

121.24220,14.16990.name: SEARCA — regional biotechnology information
121.24220,14.16990.desc: A Southeast Asian centre producing biotechnology information and training for governments across the region, in a part of the world where several countries have adopted carve-outs for edited crops within a few years of each other. Where a regional body supplies the briefing material, the regulatory texts tend to converge.

5.66400,51.98600.name: Wageningen University & Research
5.66400,51.98600.desc: The leading agricultural university in Europe and one of the largest sources of plant science anywhere, with a research funding model that ties it closely to industry. Much of the technical evidence the EU relies on when assessing crops originates in a small number of institutions of this kind, and this is the largest of them.
